reason: Details about the other three Claude windows (Sportsync AI, Alima models, architecture diagram) are irrelevant to this story and dilute the hook before the viewer knows what the story is about.
The pivot line 'the thing I actually want to walk through is this fourth window' is the natural hook that opens the story without unnecessary baggage.
Establishes all five safety constraints Mohammad gave Claude — essential context for understanding why Claude's subsequent security flag was meaningful and unprompted.
Shows Claude successfully delivered exactly what was asked, which makes the pivot to the security flag more surprising and impactful.
Browsing old GitHub templates and 'killing time' is dead filler with no story content; removing it tightens the cut directly to the discovery beat.
Core discovery beat: Claude finds real API keys in the environment and stops to flag them instead of silently using them — the central event this story is built around.
Claude's explanation of the specific threat (client-side key visible in recording, DevTools, network tab) gives the security risk concrete stakes the audience can immediately understand.
The analogy 'open door for a huge bill' lands the stakes emotionally, and Claude asking how to handle it shows collaborative rather than autonomous behavior — both important for the story's arc.
Mohammad's three explicit conditions (server-side key, never in browser, fully local) are the decision that drives the solution; necessary for the solution beat to make sense.
Shows Claude implementing the exact architecture Mohammad specified, including retaining mock files as a safety fallback — completes the solution beat cleanly.
Live demonstration of real (non-mock) English and Arabic responses proves the secure architecture works and gives the story a concrete payoff.
Lesson beat recaps the full loop concisely and names the key takeaway (Claude caught a security risk unprompted) — essential closing for the audience.
